name: The Apache Software Foundation (ASF)
origin_detail: Grew out of the 'Apache Group' of developers who extended the NCSA HTTPd web server; the ASF was incorporated on 25 March 1999 (effective 1 June 1999) in Delaware and received 501(c)(3) exemption in January 2001.
openness_notes: All projects under the permissive Apache License with meritocratic, volunteer, foundation-level governance (members elect the board).
latest_value_type: annual revenue, IRS Form 990, fiscal year ending April 2025 (expenses $2,334,727)
risk_events: FY2025 (to April 2025) deficit: revenue $2.22M vs expenses $2.33M; net assets $4.21M.
A very small budget relative to the project portfolio (290+ projects, 10,200+ committers) means the ASF relies on volunteers and employer-paid contributors rather than funding developers itself.
robustness: Extremely durable governance model (27 years) with 1,190+ members and 10,200+ committers; projects are maintained largely by contributors paid by their employers, so the foundation's small budget is not a single point of failure. Still adding top-level projects (Auron, Reqsign, ResilientDB announced 14 Oct 2026).
physical_science_relevance: Supplies the data layer for large-scale science and AI pipelines (Spark, Arrow, Parquet, Kafka) rather than domain physics codes.
openness_effect_assessment: The ASF shows that neutral, volunteer governance can steward hundreds of critical projects on about $2M a year, because value creation is distributed to employers of contributors. The same lean model means it cannot fund maintenance directly, unlike the much richer Linux Foundation.
key_takeaway: The ASF is the low-budget, high-legitimacy end of open governance: roughly $2.2M a year in revenue supports 290+ projects, about one-hundredth of the Linux Foundation's $221M. For science it is a reminder that foundation budgets measure overhead, not the value of what they steward.
